Round 2 made real progress on scope/calibration: the api-gateway 21% vs auth-service 36% gap is now explained arithmetically as a denominator/traffic-mix effect (F25/F26, T5), killing my round-1 objection that a uniform fixed-fraction failure couldn't explain the gateway number; F22/F27 exclude throttling; F28/F18/F17 confirm no downstream datastore degradation; and the team honestly downgraded the 1/3 signal to "degenerate" (F20/F24) and now carries H1/H2/H3 at ~0.40-0.44. That is much better calibrated and the H1/H2 spread has narrowed appropriately.

What has NOT changed is the core blocker: after 5 tasks and ~15 tool calls, there is still zero evidence distinguishing the three live mechanisms, and all three now sit within 0.04 confidence — i.e. the ranking is essentially arbitrary. H1 and H2 are separated only by a 1-minute timestamp difference that the 60s-resolution metric cannot resolve (both fall in the same 14:01Z->14:02Z bucket, F23), and neither has a single verified hop: H1's parser-rejects-subset claim and H2's JWKS-propagation-lag claim are both marked ASSUMED, and the automated checks flag exactly these hops as evidence-free. H3's 1/3 mechanic is explicitly shown to be non-identifiable from the metric backend (F20/F24: no per-instance, per-AZ, per-kid, no jwks_key_resolution_miss). So the deliverable "which hypothesis is the root cause" is still unanswered, not merely unconfirmed.

Crucially, this is not a case of asking for confirmation of an established result or of a permanently dead data source. Most of the failed probes were "metric dimension does not exist on the metric backend" (not_found), which is a dead end — I will not re-request those. But the routing gap I flagged in round 1 persists inside the same task types: T2 (dependency) was explicitly scoped to deployments/config only and never enumerated secret/DNS/service-mesh changes, and the team itself lists this as an open gap; and no one has tried a non-metric observability source (the team's own open question names apiserver/container events and eBPF). The budget is ~21 calls with one round left — enough for 1-3 decisive, obtainable queries. Two survive: (1) an infra/state-change sweep that could reveal a replica/AZ event at 14:01-14:02 (the H3 discriminator) or a JWKS/secrets publication change (the H2 discriminator), and (2) a per-pod container-event / process-start probe in the same window that distinguishes one-replica-failed (H3/H6) from uniform-fraction (H1/H2). If both return empty/unavailable, the incident is genuinely inconclusive and the team should say so rather than certify a 0.44 top hypothesis.

What the evidence CANNOT do is choose between the three live mechanisms. H1 (parser regression rejecting a token subset), H2 (JWKS/key-resolution lag from the rotation) and H3 (one-of-three replica/AZ failing) are each missing their one load-bearing hop, and the automated checks flag exactly those hops as evidence-free. The decisive discriminators do not exist in this environment: no per-instance/AZ/kid/issuer/tenant breakdown (F20/F24), no jwks_key_resolution_miss (F28 failed), no error-signature/status-class split (F29), no lifecycle or apiserver source (F41), and auth-service logs are permanently 503 (F13/F37). The 1/3 magnitude is explicitly non-identifiable (F24) and the H1-vs-H2 timestamp difference is below the metric's resolution (F23). H6 is additionally weakened by F31's proven single non-partial rollout, but that does not rescue the others.

This is therefore a genuine inconclusive: the data cannot separate the top hypotheses and no further query would change that. I will not accept a 0.40 top hypothesis as a root cause, and I will not send more requests — every enumerable source has been enumerated and every available discriminator is either absent from the schema or behind the dead identity pipeline.

Final round. Rounds 2-3 have now closed every routing gap I flagged: T6 enumerated ALL change sources (scope='all services' and scope='auth-service') and proved by schema — not inference — that no secret/JWKS-publication, service-mesh, DNS, autoscaler, replica-set or pod-eviction object exists in 13:50-14:10Z (F31/F32/F33); T7 confirmed no container/apiserver/pod-lifecycle/process-start source exists anywhere reachable (F40/F41) and touched the one live non-metric source (api-gateway WARN logs, F38/F39), which yields real 401s with trace IDs but carries no pod/instance attribute. Those were the correct decisive probes and they returned genuinely empty/unavailable, not "not retried". So the evidence base is now exhausted, not merely incomplete.

What the evidence DOES establish strongly: a real, sharp, stable ~36% step on auth-service's own metric backend with full request volume (F14/F15/F23), normal-but-rejecting resource profile (F10/F11), not traffic-correlated, not throttling (F22/F27), not a telemetry artifact (F14/F15/F16), not downstream (redis-cache/user-db/portfolio-service all flat, F17/F18/F28), and the gateway's 21% vs auth's 36% reconciled arithmetically as a denominator/traffic-mix effect (F25/F26/F30). The incident window contains exactly two changes, one minute apart — auth-service v7.3.0 with a breaking JWT-parser rewrite at 14:00Z (F4/F31) and a signing-key rotation at 14:01Z (F5/F32) — both falling inside the same unresolvable 60s onset bucket (F23).

What the evidence CANNOT do is choose between the three live mechanisms. H1 (parser regression rejecting a token subset), H2 (JWKS/key-resolution lag from the rotation) and H3 (one-of-three replica/AZ failing) are each missing their one load-bearing hop, and the automated checks flag exactly those hops as evidence-free. The decisive discriminators do not exist in this environment: no per-instance/AZ/kid/issuer/tenant breakdown (F20/F24), no jwks_key_resolution_miss (F28 failed), no error-signature/status-class split (F29), no lifecycle or apiserver source (F41), and auth-service logs are permanently 503 (F13/F37). The 1/3 magnitude is explicitly non-identifiable (F24) and the H1-vs-H2 timestamp difference is below the metric's resolution (F23). H6 is additionally weakened by F31's proven single non-partial rollout, but that does not rescue the others.

This is therefore a genuine inconclusive: the data cannot separate the top hypotheses and no further query would change that. I will not accept a 0.40 top hypothesis as a root cause, and I will not send more requests — every enumerable source has been enumerated and every available discriminator is either absent from the schema or behind the dead identity pipeline.

The 1/3 partition is explicitly non-identifiable: no per-instance/per-AZ series (F20/F24), no pod-lifecycle or process-start source (F41), restarts flat at 0.0 only excludes in-place restarts, not replaced pods (F40/F42). Residual variant (un-upgraded pod never cycled) cannot be tested because no lifecycle source exists (F41). It should stay ranked below H1/H2.
